summary: Production wall-clock timers: the real host switches the scheduler to monotonic wall time at attach (useWallClock); TaskRun.Sleep, background timers and App.Now advance with wall time while TestApp keeps the deterministic virtual clock unchanged.

implementation.mechanism: one time.AfterFunc armed for the earliest deadline wakes the existing host dispatcher; drive() runs runRealtime (catch the clock up, fire due timers, run queued work, re-arm); App.Shutdown stops the driver; advanceClock panics on a real-time scheduler (test-only per the pin)

deviations: deadlines stay whole milliseconds (the pin uses Duration); wall-mode deadlines round up so a sleep never ends early
the Windows threadpool timer is replaced by time.AfterFunc + the existing host wake; no native change, no new public API
